craft_notes: Sthāyin: the teacher's own voice (vakṣyāmi — I will tell). Sanskrit first: seal (thus they call) + promise + vision → L4 sets seal+promise line 1, vision line 2. Rows: row 6 silent-but-one ('they say' kept — the tradition-voice is IN the verse, not invented). Rupture: colon after 'tell' — promise held, vision released. Close: end-weight on firmness ('firm and well' — dhruvam doubled soft). Minimal pass: 'horned-pond' kept literal (the strange image must stay strange). Read aloud: line 1 talks (telling-tone), colon, line 2 shows (three beats: horned-pond, six-spoked, firm). Rejected: smoothing śṛṅgāṭaka to 'triangle' — killed: the pond's horns are the doctrine's own strangeness; 'strong' for dhruvam — killed: firm is fixedness, strength is force.

lines: This, they say, is entering. Now hear the form I tell:
a horned-pond wheel, six-spoked, standing firm and well.
l4.sanskrit_cite: eṣa praveśa ity āhū rūpaṃ vakṣyāmi cādhunā / śṛṅgāṭakanibhaṃ cakraṃ ṣaḍaraṃ cāparaṃ dhruvam

reads_against.argmap: The form is a seen wheel: triangular, six-spoked, firm.
c1_essence: Entry sealed by custom; the form shown: horned-pond wheel, six spokes, firm.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
